definitions.explanation: Europe and North America, as distinguished from East Asia.

examples.japanese: {西洋|せいよう}の{音楽|おんがく}が{好|す}きだ。
{西洋|せいよう}{料理|りょうり}を{習|なら}っている。
{西洋|せいよう}の{文化|ぶんか}に{興味|きょうみ}がある。
{西洋|せいよう}{風|ふう}の{家|いえ}に{住|す}むのが{子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}からの{夢|ゆめ}だった。
examples.english: Living in a Western-style house has been my dream since childhood.

examples.japanese: {西洋|せいよう}と{東洋|とうよう}の{文化|ぶんか}の{違|ちが}いを{研究|けんきゅう}して{論文|ろんぶん}を{書|か}いた。
examples.english: I studied the differences between Western and Eastern cultures and wrote a paper.

notes:
{西洋|せいよう} means "the West" - referring to Europe and North America, as contrasted with East Asia.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {西洋|せいよう}{人|じん}: Westerner
- {西洋|せいよう}{風|ふう}: Western-style
- {西洋|せいよう}{料理|りょうり}: Western cuisine
- {西洋|せいよう}{文化|ぶんか}: Western culture
- {西洋|せいよう}{音楽|おんがく}: Western music

CONTRAST:
- {西洋|せいよう}: the West, Western countries
- {東洋|とうよう}: the East, Eastern countries (Asia)
- {欧米|おうべい}: Europe and America (more specific)

NOTE:
{西洋|せいよう} often carries connotations of traditional Western culture, while {欧米|おうべい} is more neutral for modern Western countries.
